scope: Proposition 17.1 (Reduction to strict data) of the manuscript “Boundary graph deformations for the spacetime Penrose inequality” (preprints/Boundary-graph-deformations-for-the-spacetime-Penrose-inequality-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4205f51d8f1b130b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 114. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The data of Theorem 16.1 admit smooth approxi- mations (gj, Kj) on the same exterior such that trgj Kj = 0, µj − |Jj|gj ≥ cjr−4−δ , ΘKj (S) < 0, Rgj = O(r−4−δ ), cj > 0. (17.1) They have the prescribed O2(r−q) metric decay and O1(r−1−q) tensor decay, and all their coordinate derivatives are bounded uniformly over end patches of unit size, with constants allowed to depend on j and the derivative order. Moreover, Egj −→ Eg, Agj (S) −→ Ag(S). (17.2) Consequently, it suffices to prove Eg ≥ 1 2(Ag(S)/ω3)2/3 for such strict maximal data on this exterior. Neither vacuum nor marginality is required of the intermediate approximations.
